scope: Standing Intermediate Reservoir Valve House and footbridge, including the rounded granite shell, dressed plinth, segmenting roof strings, arched heads and cast-iron rainwater fittings.
geometryBasis: Twelve distinct vertices from government heritage map record 892 preserve the exact mapped house footprint. The surveyed dam and local path endpoint inform the reconstructed footbridge route.
sectionBasis: Standing granite valve house with a rounded lakeward front, dressed granite foundation, flat roof, arched heads and a short projecting entrance landing above the dam.
limitations: The government map fixes the valve-house footprint. Floor and roof heights, arched opening spacing and pipe details are estimates from the terrain and official appraisal.
The approach path endpoint and documented footbridge support an estimated deck run along the crest. Its precise alignment, steel details and support spacing are not surveyed.
The original 5 m survey includes the raised valve structure and sometimes meets the modeled walls above the plinth in the terrain preview.

facts.rainwater: rectangular cast-iron downpipe with ornamental hopper
